Why does repairing take more materials than crafting AND experience?

Repairing is way too expensive. Both of these are unenchanted and have never been repaired. These are examples, I don't actually want to repair them. They're the only unenchanted tools I have that weren't full durability. It should only take experience if they're enchanted, and shouldn't take more materials than crafting a new one.

text:
Minecraft combat would be a lot more satisfying if instead of poking, we swung.

How many times have you swung your sword just to not connect with mobs even at a reachable distance? That is because we don't swing swords in Minecraft; there is no physical movement. It only connects when the target is pretty much right in the middle of the crosshair. It feels more like we are poking enemies than swinging at them. This could be easily be fixable by increasing the spread.

text:
Does anyone else just refuse to make farms?

Everyone talks about having an iron farm, a gold farm, etc. Some people make bamboo farms, cactus farms, creeper farms.

I understand how (and YouTube is always an option) but to me it just takes the fun out of it. I built a sugarcane farm in one of my worlds because I wanted to fill a library with books, but I found it easier/more fun to just go find the stronghold and a mansion and loot their books. Whether that saved time or not idk.
Farms just seem like cheating to me. Not in a you-dont-deserve-your-achievements type of cheating, but a this-takes-all-of-the-fun-out-of-it cheating. Idk. I feel so much more accomplished with my stacks of iron after cave diving for a few hours versus the several chests from an iron farm. The Redstone and mechanics of farms can be pretty impressive, but to me getting resources is half the fun.
Also, farms are generally ugly. Lol. I've seen youtubers make giant builds around them so you don't have to look at them, but that in itself is just too much time and resources when I could just get all those resources over time.

Maybe I just enjoy exploring more than the people who would rather get straight to doing big builds.

text:
Minecraft desperately needs more enchantments: not stronger ones, just more interesting ones

Anyone else feel like enchanting in Minecraft has basically been solved for years?

Every survival world ends with the exact same gear:

Mending Unbreaking III Prot IV Efficiency V Sharpness V

The problem is not balance. The problem is lack of choice.
Minecraft is at its best when players solve problems differently, but enchantments barely allow different playstyles anymore. Everyone just builds the objectively correct setup.

I do not want power creep. I want weird, niche, fun enchantments that actually change gameplay.

Stuff like:

  * vein mining with durability tradeoff

  * shield enchants

  * movement based boot enchants

  * xbow/bow enchants focused on utility instead of damage

  * Elytra enchants with pros and cons
  * weapon enchants that reward timing/combat style

Also, enchant progression basically ends after villagers. Once you get a trading hall, you skip almost all loot progression forever.

Ancient Cities, Trial Chambers, End structures, mineshafts, dungeons, ocean monuments, all of them could have unique enchantments or upgrade paths worth exploring for - or even give us enchants we can only obtain using rare(r) items/blocks collected in more end game environments.
Right now enchanting feels less like building a character and more like filling out a checklist once per world. It desperately needs some thought and love.
